second_read.note: Hamiltonian H = J1 Σ si·sj + J2 Σ si·sj over NN and NNN pairs 'counting each bond once', J1 = 1, periodic boundaries; Lanczos ED, deterministic, bound_type exact. Units and J2 label checked inside the paper: E/N = 2⟨s0·s1⟩ + 2 J2 ⟨s0·s6⟩ from Table 2 (R = (1,0) and (1,1)) gives -0.677370, -1.3e-6 from the table value (the correlations are printed to 6 decimals). Cluster: the paper's Fig. 1 (vectors not printed in the text). Reconstructed from the figure's site-label coordinates and its periodic images (labels 3 and 23 repeated at a shift (2,−6), 35 and 38 at (−6,−2)): the tilted square torus T1 = (6,2), T2 = (−2,6), |T|² = 40, orthogonal, all 40 labels distinct modulo T1, T2, no mirror symmetry (point group C4). The paper's GS-sector size, 'nh = 430909650 for N = 40', equals exactly the q = (0,0), C4-irrep A, spin-flip-even dimension of that cluster by the character formula (out/VP10-heisenberg-j1j2/sector_dims.mjs; the other q = 0 sectors have 430693098 (A−), 430909268 (B+), 430693228 (B−)), which confirms the reconstruction and identifies the sector that was diagonalised. At J2 = 0 the Marshall-Peierls ground state lies in exactly this sector (the C4 rotation and the translations preserve the Marshall sign on this cluster, and spin flip is even because N_A = 20), so the sector minimum is the ground state. Only row on its instance; no duplicate. Independent recompute requested (group VE-exact-recompute has it as todo): cluster T1 = (6,2), T2 = (−2,6), sector q = 0, A, spin flip +.

verified.note: Table 2.1 (p. 102), row N = 40, edge vectors (2, 6), (-6, 2), column E0. The mirror image of the cluster of Richter & Schulenburg, EPJB 73, 117 (2010), T1 = (6, 2), T2 = (-2, 6); a reflection of the square lattice maps one onto the other, so the spectra agree. That paper prints -27.09485025, this value to one more digit. | Spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet H = J sum_<ij> S_i . S_j on the square lattice, J = 1, periodic boundaries on the finite lattice defined by the two edge vectors printed in the row (Betts construction, Sec. 2.4.1); E0 is the total singlet ground-state energy in S.S units, stored as the Pauli total 4 E0. Version read: publisher PDF (Springer, a scan), Table 2.1 on p. 102 read from the page image; identical to Table 1 of the arXiv text cond-mat/0412662. Peer review: a chapter of an edited lecture-notes volume, not a refereed journal.
